articles.title: Recounts Are Set to Take Place in Some of the Tightest Uncalled Midterms Races. How Do They Work?
articles.summary: Just over two weeks after Election Day , the outcomes of nearly all of this year’s congressional races have been determined. But a few of the tightest lower chamber races remain uncalled—and the trailing candidates in more than one are moving to request recounts. Two of those requests have come from candidates in North Carolina: Republican Representative Virginia Foxx of the state’s 5th District and Ashley Bell, a Democrat who ran in the 10th District. articles.title: School Phone Bans Show Small Learning Gains. Are They Worth It?
articles.summary: School phone bans were associated with a small but statistically significant improvement in a combined measure of math and reading achievement growth, a new report found . But the literature on the effectiveness of bans is limited, and the question remains whether modest academic improvements are worth the cost and labor involved in enforcing them. articles.title: The True Story Behind Madden and the Video Game That Turbo-Charged the NFL
articles.summary: In 1984, Trip Hawkins, founder of video-game publisher Electronic Arts (EA), boarded an Amtrak train in Denver for a meeting that would one day prove monumental. articles.title: America's Aging Air Travel Infrastructure Isn't Ready for Climate-Fuelled Extreme Weather
articles.summary: The U.S. is still reeling from a nationwide ground stop last Friday—the longest such flight stoppage in 25 years—which lasted more than four hours and resulted in more than 15,000 delayed or cancelled flights. And with Thanksgiving only a week away, the year’s busiest travel season is about to begin—bringing with it anxieties of further disruption .
